insight: If a web application sends a WebSocket message concurrently with the WebSocket connection closing, it is possible that the application will continue to use the socket after it has been closed.

impact: A local attacker can manipulate the RMI registry to perform a man-in-the-middle attack to capture user names and passwords used to access the JMX interface.

The attacker can then use these credentials to access the JMX interface and gain complete control over the Tomcat instance.

Details: Apache Tomcat RCE Vulnerability (May 2020) - Linux
Product: cpe:/a:apache:tomcat:8.5.23
Method: Apache Tomcat Detection Consolidation
insight:
If:
- an attacker is able to control the contents and name of a file on the server and
- the server is configured to use the PersistenceManager with a FileStore and
- the PersistenceManager is configured with sessionAttributeValueClassNameFilter='null' (the default unless a SecurityManager is used) or a sufficiently lax filter to allow the attacker provided object to be deserialized and
- the attacker knows the relative file path from the storage location used by FileStore to the file the attacker has control over
then, using a specifically crafted request, the attacker will be able to trigger remote code execution via deserialization of the file under their control. Note that all of conditions must be true for the attack to succeed.

detection_method: Checks if a vulnerable version is present on the target host.
impact: Apache Tomcat is prone to an information disclosure vulnerability.
insight: The simplied implementation of blocking reads and writes introduced in Tomcat 10 and back- ported to Tomcat 9.0.47 onwards exposed a long standing (but extremely hard to trigger) concurrency bug that could cause client connections to share an Http11Processor instance resulting in responses, or part responses, to be received by the wrong client.
